i think a lot of the problem is caused by mods being in charge of a subverse while having no real accountability to the subscribers. in effect this makes the mod more important than the sub. from what i understand about the way the mod system is designed it almost suggests that the subverse belongs to the mods exclusively and they can do what they damn well please with it, subscribers be damned.

don't get me wrong, most moderators are really great and deserve a lot of thanks for the time and effort they spend to allow us to have a place where conversations can take place. i can only imagine what a load of work that is and all the bull that they put up with on a day to day basis.

that being said, it seems like the mod system itself contributes to the problems when there are instances of moderators losing touch with the subverse they created, having a hissy fit because of it, and deciding to burn the whole thing down.

i think that an option that can be implemented to prevent this is a way for the subscribers of a subverse to be able to oust a mod, perhaps by a vote of confidence for example if that person no longer has the best interests of the subverse in mind. i think this would help prevent the kind of problems that the other voter-supported-aggregation-site-that-shall-remain-unnamed-because-reddit-5uxx0r5 has had. namely noxious mods taking over subs so they can control speech. these feckless mods could be ousted by the subscribers of a subverse by a vote of no confidence if the mods didn't represent the sub properly.
